_comment: Cross-runtime vectors for end-of-line padding removal. `capture-pane -J` preserves trailing spaces as the price of rejoining wrapped rows, so the daemon drops them at capture (src/shared/pane-trim.ts, trimPaneRowPadding) and the console drops them again at render (TerminalAnsi.kt, trimLineEnds). The two must never disagree about which trailing spaces are padding: over-trimming on either side deletes cells a background or reverse painted, and only a row that actually carries one shows it. Read by BOTH src/__tests__/pane-trim.test.ts and android/.../PaneTrimVectorsTest.kt. `expectText` is the surviving TEXT with every escape removed, because that is the one thing both runtimes produce: the TS half returns bytes (escapes preserved, so a later row inherits the colour state tmux emitted), while the Kotlin half returns styled runs and its text is their concatenation. The escape-level promises are TS-only and are asserted in pane-trim.test.ts rather than here. Control bytes are written as \u escapes so none sits raw in the file.

vectors.name: padding under a background stays: a coloured row paints out to the pane edge
padding under reverse stays: reverse paints a background from the foreground
a row that is only padding empties, keeping its newline
spacing inside a row is layout, not padding
padding spanning several colour changes goes entirely
a truecolor background counts as painted
a 256-colour FOREGROUND whose index is 48 is not a background
a truecolor foreground carrying 48, 7 and 44 as channels is not a background
an empty parameter is dropped, not read as a reset that would clear the background
an OSC 8 hyperlink is opaque, so a space inside its target is never padding
a non-SGR CSI is skipped without eating the character after it
colour state carries across rows, the way a capture emits it
the last row is trimmed even with no trailing newline
a row with nothing to drop is untouched
